posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
Finding out who Biomancer really is does put the answer of why he couldn't get the Philosopher's Stone to work into even more of a curiosity, though.

Aside: Bolnerap shared the Widow's Walk info with me not too long ago, and my reaction at Biomancer's real name was basically "Man that is such a cheesy name, it sounds exactly like the sort of thing a pompous magitek supervillain would call himself." So finding out it's actually a real person's name gave me sort of a bemused "reality is apparently way stranger than fiction" kind of moment.

I feel a little sad about those of my questions I sent in that didn't get answered, but on the whole I really enjoyed the episode. A creepy-as-heck villain who goes around doing weird creepy mad science and magic things just because he wants to know everything and wants to turn everything into his big master plan is exactly the sort of villain I find entertaining.

I also liked the philosophical asides (the question "what exactly qualifies as being alive in the Sentinels universe" continues to constantly produce fascinating considerations), not to mention the gigantic "buh what?" reveal.

I agree with Matchstickman's sentinement about the episode. Like, it filled time, but nothing super special came from it that was of note and made me feel, "Yeah, I'm glad this got an episode." Biomancer doesn't even feel like an important actor in the multiverse, 'cause the episode made him sound more aloof than menacing through most of his history, and none of his contributions felt like they impacted the story of the multiverse any meaningful way.

I really don't mean this as derogitory to the community or anyone else, but I almost feel like the meta stuff has escalated Biomancer to a higher level of importance than the guy ever actually had. The fans really like him, and they keep getting letters from Fleshchildren, so let's give him an episode...but not have much to say about the guy.

posts.cooked: Yeah, color me disappointed as well.  We learned a little bit about his history, but even the big story reveal was sort of, "This thing happened!  And then it was resolved and everyone lived happily every after."  Very little about his motivation or his methodology.  I was hoping for some hint about how he might handle himself in the Cosmic Contest, but it sounds like he'd be totally useless there--plopped down in person, without months to prepare fleshchildren and a nice safe place to hide his real body, it's seems like he'd be 100% helpless.  I also asked for some stories about the specific encounters with specific Fleshchildren, especially the Carbon Adept, and didn't get them.  And nothing about The Scholar--we know why Biomancer is irritated at Scholar for succeeding where he failed, but nothing about any conflicts between them or where that whole rivalry goes, if anywhere.
